Star Wars: X-Wing

Star Wars: X-Wing is a miniatures game of space combat where players pilot iconic Star Wars ships in fast-paced dogfights. The game uses pre-painted plastic ships at 1:27 ratio scale, covering everything from tiny A-Wings to the Millennium Falcon. There are no infantry-scale miniatures — every model is a vehicle or ship.

What scale am I actually printing?

Miniature Scale
1:27
Ratio Equivalent
1:27
Measurement
vehicle scale
Eye Level Height
59.3mm

X-Wing uses 1:27 ratio scale, which works out to roughly 59.3mm eye-level and 64.8mm top-of-head for a human-sized reference. Ships vary dramatically in size — a TIE Fighter is small enough to hold in your palm, while a Rebel Transport fills most of the table. Bandai and Revell sell compatible Star Wars model kits at 1:48 scale, which are slightly smaller but work for casual play.

Publisher: Atomic Mass Games·Base Sizes: Small (80mm), Medium (100mm), Large (140mm)

Printing these minis on FDM

1:27 ships are large enough for FDM to handle detail well. Use 0.2mm nozzle at 0.08mm layers for cockpit glass, panel lines, and engine details. Large ships like the Millennium Falcon benefit from 0.4mm nozzle at 0.12mm layers for speed. The smooth hull surfaces of Star Wars ships show layer lines easily, so print at the finest layer height you have patience for. Orient engines and cockpits upward to keep support marks on hidden undersides.

All settings tested on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini with PLA. Your printer may want something different — always print a test piece first.

Frequently Asked Questions

What scale is Star Wars: X-Wing?
Star Wars: X-Wing miniatures are 1:27 scale (1:27 ratio), measured vehicle scale. X-Wing uses 1:27 ratio scale, which works out to roughly 59.3mm eye-level and 64.8mm top-of-head for a human-sized reference. Ships vary dramatically in size — a TIE Fighter is small enough to hold in your palm, while a Rebel Transport fills most of the table. Bandai and Revell sell compatible Star Wars model kits at 1:48 scale, which are slightly smaller but work for casual play.
What base sizes does Star Wars: X-Wing use?
Star Wars: X-Wing uses the following base sizes: Small (80mm), Medium (100mm), Large (140mm).
What nozzle and layer height should I use for Star Wars: X-Wing miniatures?
1:27 ships are large enough for FDM to handle detail well. Use 0.2mm nozzle at 0.08mm layers for cockpit glass, panel lines, and engine details. Large ships like the Millennium Falcon benefit from 0.4mm nozzle at 0.12mm layers for speed. The smooth hull surfaces of Star Wars ships show layer lines easily, so print at the finest layer height you have patience for. Orient engines and cockpits upward to keep support marks on hidden undersides.
